audit.reasoning: The coding (fixed-dominant, final syllable: rule 01 001 0001...) rests on Meillet 1913 sec. 23, which I fetched sources from the cited archive.org item and confirmed verbatim at p. 16. Three further open sources fetched sources now agree: Thomson 1989 p. 14-15 ('always stressed on the last full syllabic', epenthetic schwa before final nasal/liquid not counted), Meillet 1903 Esquisse sec. 5 (final accent from the start of the historical period, persisting into medieval Cilician and most modern dialects), and Karst 1901 (Cilician/Middle Armenian, presupposes final = stressed). The only nuances (proclitic/enclitic unstressed words; a few adverbs/compounds like orpēs analysed by Meillet as word groups; epenthetic ə not counted) do not affect a fixed-final classification and could populate the empty 'domain'/'edge' fields ('last full vowel; epenthetic ə excluded'). sources.citation: Thomson, Robert W. 1989. An Introduction to Classical Armenian. 2nd ed. Delmar, NY: Caravan Books. (archive.org thomson1989introclassicalarmenian, Robert Bedrosian Library)
sources.quote: 'Armenian words are always stressed on the last full syllabic. Thus k'ałak', k'ałak'i (city) but astł (star), usumn (study). Some adverbs and a few other compound words have stress on the first syllable, e.g. orpēs, but nevertheless the following rules for vocalic alternation also apply to them.'

sources.citation: Meillet, Antoine. 1913. Altarmenisches Elementarbuch. Heidelberg: Carl Winter. (archive.org altarmenischesel00meil)
sources.quote: 'Die letzte Silbe ist in jedem Vollwort die betonte Silbe ... Das [ə] ... zwischen Konsonant und auslautenden Nasal oder Liquida ... wird nicht mitberechnet'; sec. 24 unstressed words (copula, indefinites, prepositions); sec. 25 apparent non-final stress = word groups with unstressed second member.

sources.citation: Meillet, Antoine. 1903. Esquisse d'une grammaire comparée de l'arménien classique. 1st ed. Vienne: Imprimerie des PP. Mékhitharistes. (archive.org EsquisseGrammaireArmenienClassique; Google scan; Glottolog lists the 1936 2nd ed.)
sources.quote: 'Par suite, tout mot arménien est, dès le début de l'époque historique, accentué sur la dernière syllabe, et cette accentuation a persisté jusqu'aujourd'hui dans la plupart des dialectes'; notes a secondary initial accent and medieval Cilician syncope (cl. hawatam > Cilician avdam 'ce qui suppose hàwatám'), i.e. final main stress also for Middle Armenian.
sources.locator: Ch. I Phonétique, I. Accentuation, sec. 5
